notes: 582 rows reviewed and inventoried under docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/inventory/. Exalted: The Lunars supplied and inventoried cover-to-cover (341 rows): the core innate powers, every Charm category in Chapter Five (pp. 122-193/PDF 125-196: Shapechanging I/II/III, Body Enhancement I/II, Unarmed Combat I-V, Melee Combat I/II, Ranged Combat I/II, Defensive I/II/III, Survival and Healing I/II/III/IV, Perception I/II/III/IV, Stealth, Interaction and Knowledge/Presence I/II/III/IV, Spirit, and Sorcery-access Charms), and all of Chapter Four: Traits (pp. 94-115/PDF 97-118): the altered Backgrounds (Artifact, Backing, Followers, Manse, Mentor), the new Backgrounds (Cult, Heart's Blood, Renown) plus a Regions sidebar, all three player Castes (Full Moon, Changing Moon, No Moon) and the Casteless state (this edition has three Castes, not the five-Caste structure from later editions), the universal Caste anima effects and Lunar Anima Banners table, the Great Curse (this splat's Limit-Trait analog) and its four Virtue-linked thralls, and the Face/Renown social-rank system. No dedicated Lunar-specific Merits/Flaws subsection or Tribe write-up exists in Exalted: The Lunars itself -- confirmed absent, not merely unreviewed. That gap is now filled by a second source: the Exalted Players Guide's Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (pp. 18-41/PDF 21-44), fully transcribed as 88 rows (44 merits + 44 flaws) applicable across all five planned Exalted families, with Lunar-specific eligibility/cost caveats (Lunars-only Chimera; Celestial-Exalted-only Known Anathema/Permanent Caste Mark/Greater Curse/Throwback; Abyssals-and-Ghosts-only Death-Taint, not applicable to Lunars) captured in each row's notes. Determining 'favored' required a genuine design decision: unlike every other family, Lunar Charms carry no single governing Ability (`ability: null` on every LunarCharmDefinition; Charms are organized by charmCategory instead, and minimumRequirements freely mix Attributes and Abilities within the same category), so the standard 'check the Charm's one Ability against favoredAbilities/Caste-Ability-group' pattern does not apply, and Lunar's three Castes are Attribute-linked rather than Ability-linked, so there is no Caste-Ability fallback either (unlike Abyssal/Sidereal). Absent any source text describing a Lunar-specific Charm-cost framework, this gap was surfaced directly to the project owner rather than guessed at; the approved design is: a Charm is Favored if ANY of its minimumRequirements traits matches one of the character's own 5 chosen Favored Abilities (the same favoredAbilities field every splat already uses), via the same normalizedAbilityId label-matching helper every other family's isXAbilityFavored already relies on. Charms whose requirements are Attribute-only (e.g. 'Manipulation 2') naturally resolve to Unfavored, since Attribute labels never match a real Ability id in favoredAbilities -- no separate Attribute-only branch was needed. Sorcery spells are keyed off Occult, the same convention Dragon-Blooded/Abyssal/Sidereal already use.
